cf.title: Extract numeric filed in JSONB more effectively

input.subject: Extract numeric filed in JSONB more effectively

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at level 1, and the support-function design follows the direction given in message #17. Three fixable level 2 points remain. The v4 to v6 mails do not show that rewritten casts return the same values and errors as master (prior-attempts-1). Nothing keeps the typed extractors and the cast functions in step later (maintenance-fit-2). The code-sharing question about JSON_VALUE from message #85 is still open (already-exists-1).

brief.title: Planner support function to speed up casts of jsonb extractions to scalars
brief.problem: A cast such as `(j->'a')::numeric` builds an intermediate jsonb from the extracted JsonbValue, then the cast function unpacks it again. The author measured this at about half the possible speed. The target users run casts of jsonb fields to numeric, bool or other number types in queries.
brief.proposed_design: The latest series (v6, five patches) attaches a SupportRequestSimplify function to the jsonb cast functions. It rewrites `cast(extract(...))` into a call to an explicit typed extractor, so SQL stays unchanged. It covers object field, array element, extract path, multi-subscript and jsonb_path_query_first(_tz), each to numeric, bool, int2, int4, int8, float4 and float8.
user_visible_surface: New SQL-callable typed extractor functions in pg_proc, such as jsonb_object_field_numeric or jsonb_array_element_int4, one per extractor family and target type.
Planner support functions set as prosupport on existing jsonb cast functions such as "numeric"(jsonb) and bool(jsonb).
EXPLAIN VERBOSE output shows the rewritten typed extractor call instead of the cast.
author_claims: Object-field casts to numeric and bool run about 2.1 to 2.2 times faster in a microbenchmark.
Users get the speedup without changing queries and without new operators.
Shared helpers and macros keep the code duplication from the many typed extractors under control.
jsonb_path_query is set-returning, so this prosupport model cannot optimize it.
Text, date and uuid targets need different semantics, so they are out of scope.
brief.thread_state: Pavel Stehule gave +1 and Dmitry Dolgov approved v1 and asked for SubscriptingRef support, which was added. Andy Fan questioned the duplication in the explicit-function approach; CI failed on v5 in the jsonpath-first path, v6 was posted, and CFbot now reports the patch needs a rebase.
unclear: The material does not show the full list of new pg_proc entries, how many functions the series adds, or whether they are documented.
The thread does not say if the error text for a type mismatch, such as "cannot cast jsonb string to type integer", stays the same as on master.
No reviewer has commented on v4 to v6, and the v6 fix for the jsonpath-first CI failure is not explained.
Peter Eisentraut's question on overlap with JSON_VALUE ... RETURNING numeric got no answer for the new series.
The material does not say if a SubscriptingRef with a non-constant subscript is rewritten.

prior_attempts.title: Add missing type conversion functions for PL/Python
prior_attempts.quote: So this patch is making some subtle changes to behavior. I don't think we want that.
prior_attempts.reason: Heikki Linnakangas found that the new tests showed changed behavior: on unpatched master, returning 100::float8 from a function declared to return int2 fails with "invalid input syntax for integer", but with the patch it succeeds. He said such behavior changes are not wanted, and the author agreed. No revised patch followed, and Michael Paquier returned the entry citing the behavior changes.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P9 changed PL/Python output conversion, not jsonb casts. It is an analogy only: a faster direct conversion path was returned because it changed results.

objections.title: Rewritten casts must behave exactly like the casts they replace
objections.failure_scenario: A user runs `(j->'a')::int2` on a value such as 1.5, 70000 or a string. The query that gets rewritten returns a different value or a different error than the same cast that is not rewritten, for example a direct call to `int2(jsonb)`. The user notices only when results or error handling differ between two forms of the same query.
objections.argument: In [P9], direct type conversions that bypassed the normal conversion path were returned because they changed results in subtle ways. Here, v4 onward drops the numeric-intermediate shape and adds direct typed extractors for int2, int4, int8, float4 and float8 (messages #109, #111). Message #67 already found one divergence in error text, and v12 restored the old text only with an extra argument. The material does not say whether v6 keeps rounding, overflow errors and error texts identical to master for every target type.
objections.author_must_show: Do tests show that every rewritten form returns the same values and the same errors as the unrewritten cast, for each target type, including rounding, overflow and type mismatch?

precedents.title: Add missing type conversion functions for PL/Python

critic.reasoning: Message #109 drops the numeric-intermediate shape, and nothing in the v4 to v6 mails says that values, overflow errors and error text match master for each target type. [P9] concerns PL/Python and serves only as an analogy; the objection stands without it.

objections.title: Typed extractors duplicate cast semantics that must stay identical
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch changes how int4(jsonb) rounds, range-checks or words its error. The 35 typed extractors keep the old behaviour. `(j->'a')::int4` then returns a different result or error depending on whether the planner rewrote it, and users first see this as a report that the same query behaves differently in a PL/pgSQL expression and in a plain query.
objections.argument: The rewrite is correct only while each typed extractor matches the existing cast exactly, and nothing makes them fail together when one changes. Messages #67 and #68 show that the error text already diverged once. The brief says it is not known whether v6 keeps errors such as "cannot cast jsonb string to type integer". In [P9], direct conversion paths were returned because they changed behaviour.
objections.author_must_show: Which mechanism, test or shared code path ensures that every typed extractor gives the same result and error as the cast it replaces, for every target type?

precedents.title: Add missing type conversion functions for PL/Python

critic.reasoning: The series does not say whether the typed extractors share conversion and error code with the jsonb cast functions, so a later change to one can miss the other. The PL/pgSQL detail is weak, since message #45 concedes those expressions are planned too.

objections.title: Second fast path overlaps JSON_VALUE ... RETURNING without shared code
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch changes how jsonb scalars become numeric or bool, for example error codes or int2 overflow text. It updates the JSON_VALUE RETURNING path but misses the many typed extractors, or the reverse. Users then get different errors for `(j->'a')::int2` and `json_value(j, '$.a' returning int2)`, and only bug reports show it.
objections.argument: Message #85 shows JSON_VALUE ... RETURNING numeric already extracts a typed scalar without the jsonb round trip, and asks whether this patch should reuse or share code with it. Message #86 answers with one benchmark where the patch is faster (1.75 ms against 2.59 ms) and says code sharing is unclear. The v6 series, with five extractor families and seven target types, does not answer that question. A committer would likely ask why the support function cannot rewrite to the existing JSON_VALUE machinery, or why that machinery cannot be made faster and reused, before many single-purpose pg_proc entries are added.
objections.author_must_show: Why can the support function not rewrite into the existing JSON_VALUE RETURNING machinery, or share its scalar conversion code, and what is the measured cost of doing so?

critic.reasoning: Message #86 answers question 3a of message #85 only with "not sure if we could share some code", and the v4 to v6 mails add jsonb_path_query_first without returning to it. The error-drift scenario is weak, because the two spellings already differ on master.

refuted.title: Typed extractors may change cast results and errors for existing queries
refuted.failure_scenario: An application runs (j->'qty')::int2 or (j['flag'])::bool over existing data, and on master it gets either an error or a value from the jsonb cast function. After upgrade, the planner swaps in a typed extractor with its own conversion code, so out-of-range values, rounding, JSON null or a type mismatch can give a different result or error text. Users see the change only on bad rows, in production.
refuted.argument: The rewrite replaces the full cast path with new code for seven target types across five extractor families, and the semantics must match jsonb_int2, jsonb_int4, jsonb_float4 and the others for every input. Message #67 already found a changed error message in one form, and v6 (message #114) has an unexplained CI failure in the jsonpath-first path. The brief notes the thread does not confirm that error text and SQLSTATE stay the same. [P9] was returned because a direct-conversion shortcut changed what users got for the same input.
refuted.author_must_show: Does a test compare master and patched output, including error text and SQLSTATE, for every family and target type on JSON null, strings, out-of-range numbers and fractional values?

precedents.title: Add missing type conversion functions for PL/Python

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of prior-attempts-1. This version also misplaces the CI failure, which was on v5; v6 was posted as the fix.

refuted.title: Dozens of new SQL-callable functions become a public contract
refuted.failure_scenario: A user sees jsonb_object_field_int4 in EXPLAIN VERBOSE output and starts to call it directly in views and application SQL. Later the project wants to merge or rename these helpers, or move to a different rewrite target, and it cannot without breaking those views and pg_dump output that names them.
refuted.argument: Message #17 accepted helper functions only with the expectation that users do not call them, and messages #36 and #50 discussed keeping them internal. The v6 series exposes one function per family and type, about 35 entries, as normal SQL-callable functions shown in EXPLAIN. Message #113 defends the catalog footprint as the cleanest tradeoff, but it does not say whether these functions are documented, supported, or protected from direct use.
refuted.author_must_show: Are the typed extractors meant to be a supported user interface, and if not, what keeps users from depending on them through views and dumps?

critic.reasoning: Message #17 accepts SQL-callable helpers "under the hood", and messages #90 and #94 ask for explicit pg_proc functions. The rewrite runs at plan time, so stored views and pg_dump keep the cast unless a user writes the undocumented function by hand.

refuted.title: Overlap with the standard JSON_VALUE ... RETURNING is not addressed
refuted.failure_scenario: A user who writes json_value(j, '$.a' returning numeric), the SQL-standard way, gets slower execution than the non-standard (j->'a')::numeric. The project then keeps two separate typed-extraction code paths with different error behavior. Fixes made to one path do not reach the other.
refuted.argument: Message #85 asked whether the internal rewrite should use or share code with JSON_VALUE, which gives standard typed extraction with defined ON ERROR behavior. Message #86 answered with a benchmark for the old v18 design only, and the v4 to v6 series does not discuss it. A committer would likely ask why the fast path is built beside the standard feature and not into it.
refuted.author_must_show: Why should the cast rewrite not lower to the JSON_VALUE ... RETURNING machinery, or share its conversion code, so both spellings behave and perform the same?

critic.reasoning: Messages #86 and #87 answer the desirability part: JSON_VALUE requires users to rewrite queries, which message #17 rejects, and it measured slower. Casts and JSON_VALUE already differ in error behavior on master through ON ERROR, so the patch does not create that split.

refuted.title: About 35 new SQL-callable functions become permanent catalog API
refuted.failure_scenario: A user finds jsonb_object_field_int4 in \df and calls it in views. A later release wants to drop or merge these extractors, for example in favour of JSON_VALUE or a generic mechanism. Removing them then breaks those views, and pg_dump output from older servers no longer restores.
refuted.argument: Five extractor families times seven target types gives about 35 pg_proc entries, and each new family or target type adds seven or five more. Tom Lane in message #17 accepted helper functions only on the condition that users are not expected to call them. In v6 they are ordinary SQL-callable functions, and the material does not say whether they are documented, hidden or marked internal. Message #113 says the catalog footprint is the cleanest tradeoff, but it does not address how the project could ever take these functions back.
refuted.author_must_show: Are the typed extractors documented and supported user API, and if they are internal, what keeps users and pg_dump from depending on them?

refuted.title: Overlap with JSON_VALUE ... RETURNING not answered for the new series
refuted.failure_scenario: Core ends up with two separate fast paths for typed scalar extraction from jsonb, one in jsonpath execution and one in about 35 typed extractors. Later work on numeric or bool conversion has to update both, and the two paths drift apart in edge cases.
refuted.argument: In message #85 Peter Eisentraut asked whether this patch is still needed next to JSON_VALUE, and whether the rewrite should share code with it. Message #86 answered with a benchmark for the 2024 patch only. The v4 to v6 series reworked the design and added jsonb_path_query_first, which is the closest case to JSON_VALUE. The series does not discuss the question again.
refuted.author_must_show: Can the rewrite target JSON_VALUE's typed path or share its conversion code, and if not, why must core keep two separate implementations?

refuted.title: Full type and extractor matrix rests only on microbenchmarks
refuted.failure_scenario: The series adds one pg_proc entry for each pair of five extractor families and seven target types, so every future jsonb extraction change must update these entries too. If real queries spend most of their time detoasting large documents, the 2x gain shrinks to a few percent, and the project carries the catalog surface for little user benefit.
refuted.argument: The only numbers are microbenchmarks on tiny documents such as '{"a": 1}' (messages #1, #23, #95, #86). No field report or production workload is shown, and nothing shows that anyone casts jsonb_path_query_first to int2 or float4. The demand that is shown is reviewers agreeing the common cast syntax should be fast (messages #9, #17). That supports object-field casts to numeric and bool, but it does not by itself justify the full matrix in message #113.
refuted.author_must_show: How much faster is an end-to-end query on realistic, larger or toasted jsonb documents, and which of the seven target types and five families do users cast in practice?

critic.reasoning: Reviewers asked for the breadth: message #17 names array indexing and nested fields, #29 names array element and extract path, #100 names subscripting, and #9 lists the existing casts. A smaller gain on toasted documents is not a failure, and non-users pay no run-time cost.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: The series adds typed extractor rows to pg_proc.dat, sets prosupport on existing jsonb cast functions and bumps catversion.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch changes src/include/utils/jsonb.h, which extensions include.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: A SupportRequestSimplify function rewrites cast(extract(...)) into a typed extractor call at plan time, visible in EXPLAIN VERBOSE.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: One typed extractor per extractor family and target type must stay identical to the matching jsonb cast function.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: JSON_VALUE ... RETURNING already extracts typed scalars, and the series does not share code with it.

questions: Do tests show that every rewritten form returns the same values and errors as the unrewritten cast, for each target type, on rounding, overflow, JSON null and type mismatch?
Do the typed extractors call the same conversion and error code as the jsonb cast functions, or do they carry their own copy?
Why can the support function not rewrite into the JSON_VALUE ... RETURNING machinery or share its scalar conversion code, and what would that cost in speed?
Does the support function rewrite a SubscriptingRef whose subscript is not a constant?
What did v6 change to fix the v5 CI failure in the jsonb_path_query_first path?

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows the jsonb cast and jsonpath execution code and planner support functions. The brief says no reviewer has commented on v4 to v6.
committability.liability: The owner signs for each typed extractor matching its jsonb cast function in values and errors, for as long as both exist. The owner also signs for the new pg_proc rows.
committability.author_follow_up: The CommitFest entry lists a second author who posted v4 to v6 and a fix after the v5 CI failure. The patch has needed a rebase since 2026-11-09.

priority.reason: Casts of jsonb fields to numbers and bool are common, and the author measured about 2 times faster on small documents. The five-patch series touches jsonb.c, jsonfuncs.c, jsonpath_exec.c and pg_proc.dat, needs a rebase, and has had no review since v4.

provisional_note: Without the code, nobody can confirm that the typed extractors match the casts on every input. That also decides whether expression indexes over `(j->'a')::numeric` stay valid. The leakproof marking and the safety of direct SQL calls to the new functions are also unchecked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Jsonb transform for pl/python
precedents_retrieved.summary: A set of extensions (jsonb_plpythonu, jsonb_plpython2u, jsonb_plpython3u) implementing a CREATE TRANSFORM for jsonb in PL/Python, mapping jsonb objects to dicts, arrays to lists, and numerics to Python Decimal via string conversion, and back. The transform works in both directions so functions can take and return jsonb as native Python values.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The reviewer objected that the third version turned unsupported Python objects such as set() into JSON strings instead of raising an error, asked for tests and errors for complex numbers and ranges, and reported that the tests failed on Python 3. The author sent no revised version after that review, and the commitfest manager returned the patch with feedback because it still needed work and had had no updates for more than a week.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So this still needs more work.. I am marking it as returned with
feedback as there has been no updates for more than 1 week.

precedents_retrieved.title: jsonb array-style subscription
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add array-style subscripting to jsonb, so that values can be read with expressions like test_json['a']['a1'] and updated with assignments like UPDATE ... SET test_json['a']['a1']['a2'] = 42. The work-in-progress patch did this by extending the existing ArrayRef node, using the parser's hard-coded array subscript handling, to cover jsonb.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The early messages raise design concerns: using array syntax as key/value syntax, update assignments creating missing intermediate objects, and the lack of an operator that could use a GIN index. The visible messages end in August 2015 and the decision was in March 2016, so the shown text does not connect any of these concerns to the outcome.

precedents_retrieved.title: Collecting statistics about contents of JSONB columns
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a jsonb_typanalyze function that extracts every path from sampled JSONB documents and stores per-path statistics as an array of JSONB documents in pg_statistic under a new stakind. It also adds an "oprstat" procedure for operators such as ->> so the planner can derive statistics for expressions on JSONB columns.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tests showed ANALYZE becoming much slower: about 28 seconds against 120 ms on one data set, and over 2 hours or OOM on documents with about 850k distinct paths, because the patch loops over all sample rows once per path. The reviewers agreed the design of collecting statistics for every path in every JSONB column needs rethinking, for example by keeping only the most common paths or enabling the statistics per column. Nikita Glukhov posted optimizations and planned common-path collection, but in the last week of the commitfest the patch no longer applied and Greg Stark asked for a rebase.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: From these points, we can say that we should rethink our design to collect stats for all paths.

precedents_retrieved.title: Precision loss casting float to numeric
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Robert Haas, Bear Giles
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make the float4 and float8 to numeric casts keep full binary precision, so that the cast and the round trip back to float no longer lose bits. The proof-of-concept patch printed values with FLT_DECIMAL_DIG and DBL_DECIMAL_DIG digits in place of FLT_DIG and DBL_DIG, and the author planned a frexp-based conversion.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane and Robert Haas expected more complaints about results such as 1.1::float8 casting to an odd-looking numeric than benefit from exact values, and Bear Giles asked that existing results not change. Making the cast follow extra_float_digits would make it stable instead of immutable. Per-schema casts cannot work because casts have no names, which left a separate named function as the remaining option. The author marked the entry Returned with feedback, citing the backward-compatibility issues and lack of time in this CF.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think there's probably a bigger chance of complaints that "casting 1.1::float8 to numeric now produces some weird, incorrectly-rounded result" than that we make anyone happier.

precedents_retrieved.title: CAST( ... ON DEFAULT)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch extends CAST with NULL ON ERROR, DEFAULT expr ON ERROR and ERROR ON ERROR clauses, following syntax Vik Fearing planned to propose to the SQL committee. It builds on the error-safe user functions work and reuses CoalesceExpr in a new error-test mode to return the fallback value when the cast fails.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane did not want to extend the CAST grammar before the SQL committee standardized it, since the committee might adopt something that conflicts. Vik Fearing had not yet submitted his paper and agreed the syntax should wait until it passed the committee. Tom Lane concluded it could not go into v16, and the commitfest manager marked it Rejected; the author plans to resume once the committee acts.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm not sure that extending CAST is a great idea, because I'm afraid
that the SQL committee will do something that conflicts with it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add numeric_trim(numeric)
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Dean Rasheed, Alvaro Herrera, Robert Haas
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a function numeric_trim(numeric) that removes trailing zeros after the decimal point by lowering the value's display scale. Reviewers also discussed a minscale() function that returns the smallest scale needed, to be used with round().
precedents_retrieved.objection: Dean Rasheed found a bug: numeric_trim(1e100) fails with "value overflows numeric format" because the computed dscale goes negative. He also asked for a simpler implementation based on strip_var(), and the thread moved toward a minscale() design. The author did not post a new version, so Alvaro Herrera and later Robert Haas closed the entry as returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think this patch got useful feedback but we never saw a followup
version posted.  I closed it as returned-with-feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Direct converting numeric types to bool
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds direct casts to boolean from smallint, bigint, real, double precision and numeric, like the existing integer::bool cast. The stated goal was easier migration from Oracle.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane questioned whether the behavior is wanted, saying Oracle compatibility alone is not a reason and he recalled no migration complaints. Pavel Stehule voted -1: a cast from double to boolean makes no sense, a SQL function or an extension can do the same, and Oracle needed such tricks only because it long lacked a boolean type. Alex Ignatov noted that casting through int (1::bigint::int::boolean) already works.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Oracle has it" is not a good argument
in my view, nor do I recall people complaining that they need such
a behavior to migrate.

roaster_notes.note: Within the thread, the first design (a new operator, message #1) was dropped after objections in messages #7 and #17. The current support-function design is the one Tom Lane suggested in message #17, so that earlier rejection does not apply.

The proposal changes no on-disk format, WAL record, replication stream, wire message or extension-visible struct. Its only persistent footprint is new built-in pg_proc rows and prosupport on existing jsonb cast functions, which pg_upgrade and pg_dump handle like any built-in function. One point needs the code to confirm: expression indexes and generated columns over `(j->'a')::numeric` must yield identical values on both paths, or indexes built before the upgrade would no longer match what new queries compute.

The latest design does not touch privileges. It rewrites existing casts into new typed extractor functions that read the same jsonb value and return the same scalar, so the caller sees nothing new. The internal-return type-safety issue (messages #36, #37) no longer applies, because v6 uses typed functions. Two points need the code to confirm: that the new functions are not marked leakproof, which would change pushdown past security barrier views and RLS quals, and that direct SQL calls cannot crash, as they did in message #48.
Hot-path cost for non-users looks small: the support function runs once at plan time and only on jsonb casts.
The base need is not met by `(j->'a')::numeric` at the same speed, and JSON_VALUE requires query changes, so the only objection from this angle is overlap with JSON_VALUE.

Demand for the basic idea is reasonable: several reviewers, including Tom Lane in message #17, want the common cast syntax to be fast without query changes. The objection covers only the breadth of the series.
